name: hash_rotl_32
prose: static inline uint32_t hash_rotl_32(uint32_t x, int8_t r). Precondition: 0 < r < 32 (r == 0 would shift x right by 32 and a negative or larger r shifts by an out-of-range amount; both are undefined). name: operator new(std::size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &)
prose: operator new(std::size_t size, const std::nothrow_t &) noexcept. Precondition: none on the caller beyond a valid size. Postcondition: returns newImpl<true>(size), i.e. imalloc_fastpath(size, fallback_impl<true>), which on the fast path returns a block of at least size bytes and on failure calls malloc_default and then handleOOM(size, true). The result is a pointer to storage the caller releases with operator delete, or nullptr if allocation fails and no new handler succeeds. It is declared noexcept, so no exception leaves it: a failure is reported as nullptr, and an exception other than std::bad_alloc thrown by a user new-handler would hit the noexcept boundary and call std::terminate. Failure handling is in the static handleOOM(size, nothrow): if opt_experimental_infallible_new is set it calls safety_check_fail, which aborts by default (a registered abort hook could return, in which case handleOOM returns nullptr); otherwise it repeatedly reads the current std::new_handler under a mutex, stops if there is none, calls it (stopping if it throws std::bad_alloc; any other exception it throws propagates), and retries with je_malloc(size) until a block is obtained; if still null it throws std::bad_alloc when the nothrow flag is false (via std::__throw_bad_alloc) and returns nullptr when it is true.
note: reviewer WRONG: it is the nothrow variant; failure returns nullptr (line 89-91 with nothrow=true); I added qualifications (infallible_new abort, handler exceptions)

name: migrate_schema_step
prose: static void migrate_schema_step(const fs::path& file, int version_from, int version_to, optional<int64_t> action_id = none, optional<fs::path> old_database = none) in an anonymous namespace. Precondition: version_to == version_from + 1 (PRE, an assertion when enabled); the caller expects the database to be at version_from, which this function does not check. Postcondition: logs the step, opens file read-write with store::detail::open_and_setup, locates the migration file for (version_from, version_to) with store::detail::migration_file and reads it; if reading throws std::runtime_error it throws store::error('Cannot read migration file ...'). If action_id is set it replaces every '@ACTION_ID@' in the SQL with the id; if old_database is set it replaces every '@OLD_DATABASE@' with the path text. It then executes the SQL with db.exec; a sqlite::error is rethrown as store::error('Schema migration failed: ...'). No rollback is done by this function, so a failure in the middle of the SQL may leave earlier statements applied. Errors from opening the database or locating the migration file are not translated here and propagate as thrown. The database handle is released when the function returns or throws. Returns nothing.

name: redirect_index
prose: static int redirect_index(lutok::state& state) (lua_module.cpp lines 193-244), installed as the __index metamethod of configuration tables; on entry the stack top holds the table at index -2 and the field name at index -1. If -2 is not a table it throws config::value_error; if -1 is not a string it throws config::value_error. Otherwise: (1) it pushes '_' + field and raw-gets it from the table; if that is non-nil it returns 1 with that value on top of the stack (the table and field name are still below it). (2) Otherwise it raw-gets table[field]; if that is non-nil it returns 1 with that value on top. (3) Otherwise the field is undefined: it gets the global tree from the registry (config::syntax_error if the 'tree' entry is nil), computes the dotted key with get_tree_key (config::invalid_key_error if the field name starts with '_'; if the table has a 'tree_key' metafield the key is that prefix + '.' + field, otherwise the field alone). If tree.is_set(key), tree.push_lua pushes the recorded value and the function returns 1 with it on top (table and field still below it). If the key is not set, it creates a new table (with __index = redirect_index, __newindex = redirect_newindex and tree_key = key metadata), stores it with raw_set into the original table under '_' + field, and returns 1; in this last branch the original table and field name have been removed from the stack, leaving only the new table. In all successful paths it returns 1. Exceptions from the tree (is_set, push_lua) or the Lua state propagate, and the stack may then hold extra entries.

name: datetime::operator<<(std::ostream& output, const delta& object)
prose: std::ostream& utils::datetime::operator<<(std::ostream& output, const delta& object). Precondition: output is a usable output stream. Postcondition: writes object.to_microseconds() (seconds * 1000000 + useconds, as an int64_t, in decimal) followed by the characters 'us' to output and returns a reference to output. Stream errors are reported through the stream state (failbit/badbit) and, if the stream has exceptions enabled in its exception mask, or on allocation failure, the insertion can throw; this function does not catch anything.

name: format::formatter::formatter(const std::string& format, const std::string& expansion, const std::string::size_type last_pos)
prose: Constructor format::formatter::formatter(const std::string& format, const std::string& expansion, std::string::size_type last_pos). Precondition: last_pos <= the expansion length (a larger last_pos makes strip_double_percent's substr throw std::out_of_range). Postcondition on success: _format = format, _expansion = expansion (with the '%%' collapsing described below), _last_pos = last_pos, _oss holds a newly allocated std::ostringstream. The constructor body calls init(): find_next_placeholder scans the expansion from _last_pos, skipping '%%' pairs, for a '%'; if none is found the placeholder is empty and its position is the expansion length; the placeholder text runs from that '%' up to the first 's'. strip_double_percent then replaces every '%%' in the part between _last_pos and the placeholder with '%'; _expansion is set to the resulting string, _placeholder_pos to the placeholder's index in it (original index minus the number of removed '%'), _placeholder to the placeholder text, and _oss to new_ostringstream(placeholder): a plain stream if the placeholder is empty or 2 characters ('%s'), otherwise a stream with fill '0' if the text between '%' and 's' starts with '0', width from the digits before an optional '.', and, if a '.' is present, fixed floatfield and the precision parsed after it. It throws format::bad_format_error (and constructs no object; _oss is still NULL so nothing leaks) if the scan finds a '%' as the last character ('Trailing %'), if there is no 's' after the '%' or another '%' occurs inside the placeholder ('Unterminated placeholder'), or if the width or precision text is not a valid int. Other exceptions such as std::bad_alloc can also propagate. The destructor later deletes _oss.
note: verified against init(), find_next_placeholder, strip_double_percent, new_ostringstream; added that the placeholder ends at the first 's' and the last_pos precondition detail
